subject: StormLake launch — temporary ingress uplift & traffic shaping ask
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@stormlake.com, procure@stormlake.com
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: StormLake launch — temporary ingress uplift & traffic shaping ask

Team —

We have the StormLake production go-live scheduled for next Tuesday and the customer is expecting a predictable ramp with a 6x peak over baseline for the first 72hrs. Key asks from them (and from AE/Sales):

- Short-term quota uplift for the launch window (48–72 hours) to avoid 429s while they warm up.
- Temporary higher concurrency/rate for the "query" route (they're making many short prompt calls).
- Routing/variant guidance to keep latency under 250ms P50 for their interactive flows.

I've attached a first-pass mutual action plan and their traffic forecast. Quick asks from infra/product:

1) Can we approve a scoped rate uplift for StormLake for Sept 14–16? If yes: preferred method (temporary policy toggle vs. manual entitlement).
2) Any model-variant recommendations for preserving latency while keeping cost down? They are currently on redwood/gpt-mid-3b.
3) Any guidance on prefix caching or batching knobs that CS should ask them to implement immediately?

I'll coordinate the customer-facing messaging and the canary plan when we have alignment.

Thanks —
Monica
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0194

Attachments: StormLake_MutualActionPlan_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 132KB), stormlake_ingress_forecast_q4.csv (csv, 28KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StormLake launch — temporary ingress uplift & traffic shaping ask

Thanks Monica — quick clarifying questions before I scope infra work: 

- Is the 6x peak a short spike (10–15 minute peaks) or a sustained 6x for hours? The forecast csv hints at both.
- Do they need higher tokens/sec or higher requests/sec? For short prompts, requests/sec is the limiter.
- Do they have hard SLA requirements (P99 latency or availability targets) for the launch?

From an implementation standpoint we can do either a temporary entitlement (fast) or schedule a policy change that auto-reverts (safer). If this is a 48–72h window and they can tolerate a manual revert, I prefer the entitlement toggle so we don't leave policy drift.

Also: if they can pin to a lower-latency variant (redwood/gpt-mid-3b-opt) and enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts, we'll reduce pressure significantly. Neha — can CS confirm whether StormLake can push a small client-side cache?

I'll tentatively reserve a pool bump but need green from CS on traffic shape and from product on acceptable variant.

-karthik
Senior Infra PM

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@stormlake.com, procure@stormlake.com
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StormLake launch — temporary ingress uplift & traffic shaping ask

Karthik — good questions. I pulled a more granular forecast from the customer and re-attached (stormlake_ingress_forecast_q4.csv). Key notes from the customer call: 

- They expect a ramp that hits sustained 6x for ~4 hours on day 1, then settles to ~2–3x for the next 48 hours with short spikes.
- Requests/sec is the concern: average prompt length is ~60 tokens, most calls are <1s.
- No hard P99 SLA requested; they want to avoid visible 429s and keep P50 < 250ms.

Customer is open to pinning to a lower-latency variant and will add small client-side caching for identical initial system prompts. I've highlighted the mutual action plan with a "temporary entitlement" option as our preference for speed.

Customer comments (ops@stormlake.com):
> We really need a short runway without throttling so our ops team can stabilize traffic. We can revert to normal usage after Monday. — Rowan, StormLake

Monica

Attachments: stormlake_ingress_forecast_q4.csv (csv, 32KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@stormlake.com, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StormLake launch — temporary ingress uplift & traffic shaping ask

Adding a CS perspective and quick playbook suggestions: 

- Ask the customer to implement client-side dedupe for identical system prompts (we saw 18% reduction in similar cases).
- Increase their retry/backoff on 429s to give infra time to scale — but we want to avoid surfaced failures during the first 4 hours.
- We should prepare a rollback message for them so they can gracefully throttle if we need to revert earlier.

Operationally I'd like a canary that routes 10% of traffic through the uplifted entitlement for the first 30 minutes, then 30% for next 90, then full for the window if metrics look good. That avoids a hard flip.

I'll own the customer communication cadence during the window. If product/infra can give us the entitlement toggle window and expected provisioning time (minutes), CS will coordinate the canary steps with them.

-Neha
Customer Success Manager
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@stormlake.com
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StormLake launch — temporary ingress uplift & traffic shaping ask

All —

We can support a scoped temporary entitlement for Sept 14 00:00–Sept 16 23:59 PST for StormLake. Details: 

- Entitlement change will be applied at the tenant level and can be rolled back manually. Provisioning time ~ 7–10 minutes once we flip.
- We'll set the uplift to +5x requests/sec on their primary route (query) and enable a higher concurrency cap for their API key.
- We'll also create the canary routing rule Neha suggested (10% -> 30% -> 100%) as a traffic-splitting policy tied to the entitlement, and monitor P50/P95 latency and 429 rate.

Operational asks from CS: provide exact UTC window & the contact on-call during the launch. From Sales: sign-off on the mutual action plan and the temporary billing treatment for the uplift (we'll log usage normally; billing discussion to be captured in the MAP).

I'll create the entitlement and the canary rule in the staging account first and share the runbook link.

-aditya
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Related runbook: https://incidents.redwood.ai/runbooks/stormlake-2027-launch (staging link)
